studies.title: Deep learning reveals antibiotics in the archaeal proteome
studies.authors: Torres, Wan and de la Fuente-Nunez
studies.organism_context: Peptides mined from archaeal proteomes; activity tested against bacterial pathogens
studies.scope: Direct archaeal sequence application with selected experimental follow-up
studies.supported_claim: The study mined 233 archaeal proteomes and prioritized 12,623 candidates; 75 of 80 selected synthesized peptides were active against at least one tested bacterial strain.
studies.boundary: The hit rate concerns a selected test set, not all predicted candidates. Mouse-model evidence is not human clinical efficacy or proof of a natural antimicrobial role in archaea.
studies.locator: Results: Deep-learning-guided identification; Antimicrobial activity; abstract
studies.read_depth: Metadata, abstract and selected Results passages
studies.question: Which denominator does the reported hit rate use, and which claim would require a new experiment?

studies.title: Histone diversity in the archaeal domain of life
studies.organism_context: Archaeal histone sequence diversity across GTDB release 220
studies.method: Physicochemical-feature clustering, AlphaFold3 and molecular dynamics
studies.supported_claim: The study combines archaeal histone clustering with structural predictions and simulations; some predicted nucleosome-like arrangements are unstable in simulations.
studies.boundary: Prediction plus simulation is still computational evidence. It does not establish how the proposed assemblies organize DNA in living archaeal cells.
studies.locator: Results: structural prediction; Fig. 5; Discussion; Methods: Structural prediction
studies.read_depth: Metadata and selected Results, Discussion and Methods passages
studies.question: Are two computational analyses independent experimental confirmation? What biological observation is still missing?

studies.title: Genome modelling and design across all domains of life with Evo 2
studies.organism_context: Multi-domain genomic data, including archaeal gene-essentiality benchmarks
studies.method: Genomic foundation model; zero-shot scores for premature-stop perturbations
studies.scope: General model with a reported archaeal evaluation component
studies.supported_claim: The paper reports zero-shot gene-essentiality predictions evaluated against experimental labels across bacterial, archaeal and phage species.
studies.boundary: An archaeal benchmark is more than training-set inclusion, but it is not evidence that generated archaeal genomes are viable or that every lineage and task generalizes.
studies.locator: Fig. 2j; gene-essentiality Results paragraph; Extended Data Fig. 3h
studies.read_depth: Metadata, selected Results and figure-caption passages
studies.question: Which evidence supports an archaeal prediction task, and which broader design claim remains unsupported?

studies.title: Jumbo circular extrachromosomal elements of methane-oxidizing archaea with variably extensive metabolic and defense gene repertoires
studies.date_precision: Year only in this teaching registry
studies.method: Genome/transcript evidence with ColabFold and AlphaFold3 structure models
studies.scope: AI-assisted archaeal annotation within an integrated biological study
studies.supported_claim: The study combines genomic and expression evidence for archaeal extrachromosomal elements and deposits custom ColabFold/AlphaFold3 models alongside its data.
studies.boundary: A predicted fold, a transcribed gene and a measured metabolic effect are different evidence objects; do not infer a change in methane turnover from a model alone.
studies.locator: Abstract; Results: ECE-host association; Data availability
studies.read_depth: Selected primary HTML passages and PDF abstract/data-availability passages
studies.question: What establishes host association, and what additional evidence would establish an encoded gene's physiological effect?

studies.title: Comparative analysis of adhesin-like proteins from Methanobacteriales species
studies.organism_context: Methanobacteriales, including intestinal and rumen lineages
studies.method: AlphaFold-assisted structural analysis and PRISM domain recognition
studies.supported_claim: The paper maps adhesin-like protein architectures across 17 species and describes curated model-assisted domain recognition.
studies.boundary: Proteins exceeding 5,000 residues were excluded from prediction. PRISM is described as a manuscript in preparation; its executable release was not verified here. Domain labels do not prove adhesion mechanisms.
studies.locator: Methods: Sequence retrieval and structural modeling; Characterization of ALP domains; Discussion
studies.read_depth: Metadata, abstract and selected Methods/Discussion passages
studies.question: How do sequence-length filtering, reference annotations and split design limit a biological claim?

studies.title: Rapid and accurate prediction of protein homo-oligomer symmetry using Seq2Symm
studies.scope: General predictor applied to an archaeal proteome
studies.supported_claim: Seq2Symm was applied to the Pyrococcus furiosus proteome as part of a multi-proteome analysis.
studies.boundary: Proteome-scale predictions are not independent physical validation of every archaeal oligomer.
studies.question: Which assemblies have independent experimental references, rather than only a predicted distribution?

studies.title: A realistic phantom dataset for benchmarking cryo-ET data annotation
studies.organism_context: General cryo-ET phantom benchmark, not an archaeal-specific validation
studies.method: Experimental phantom images with curated particle annotations
studies.supported_claim: The phantom benchmark links tomograms and curated annotations; the authors explicitly acknowledge incomplete labels and possible false positives.
studies.boundary: Curated ground truth is not absolute, and performance on a phantom does not establish archaeal cellular segmentation or molecular identity.
studies.locator: Results: dataset quality and ground-truth limitations; CryoET Data Portal deposition 10310
studies.question: What can a phantom benchmark validate, and what domain-shift checks are still needed?
